title: Game mode Tactical Combat preference missing
reality: v2.3.0 added a Combat Preference to Game mode, chosen in the setup wizard and changeable later from Chat Settings -> Combat Style: classic narrative combat or a new tactical battle style on a terrain-painted battlefield with scene-matched backdrops, unit classes, party formations, per-unit movement/attack ranges, counters, crits, misses, and a full enemy phase driven by a deterministic seeded engine at four difficulty levels (animated movement, damage popups, draggable unit inspector, staged translucent move previews, restartable encounters, mobile layout). The v2.3.0 What's New spotlights it as a headline feature.
fix: In the Game Mode section of references/architecture.md, after the v2.0 state-machine paragraph (which only says 'Tactical combat UI'), add a '**Tactical Combat (v2.3)**' paragraph describing the Combat Preference (setup wizard + Chat Settings -> Combat Style), narrative vs tactical choice, terrain battlefield, deterministic seeded engine, and the 4 difficulty levels.

title: Game setup export is now importable .marinara-game-setup.json
reality: architecture.md (Session History v2.2) says Initial Game Setup 'exports the complete campaign setup as a .txt'. Since v2.3.2 (#3701) Initial Game Setup downloads produce versioned `.marinara-game-setup.json` bundles that can refill the New Game wizard, remap available local resources, warn about missing ones, and require a replacement GM connection when necessary.
fix: Update the Session History paragraph in the Game Mode section: replace the '.txt export' claim with the v2.3.2 `.marinara-game-setup.json` export/import bundle behavior (versioned, re-imports into the New Game wizard, resource remapping, missing-resource warnings, replacement GM connection prompt).

title: Hierarchical Maps package undocumented
reality: Hierarchical Maps exists nowhere in architecture.md. In v2.3.0 it became a downloadable optional package (classified as a Tracker Agent in Download Agents) enable-able in Roleplay and during/after Game creation; v2.3.2 moved its controls inside its Chat Settings -> Agents entry (#3679); v2.3.3 made it obey each chat's Enable Agents master toggle across UI/prompt/lorebook/retries/tracker patches/carryover/checkpoints, quarantined incompatible 1.0.x runtimes (t.select crash), fixed the v2.3.2 migration that wrongly auto-selected Maps in every chat (#3723), and stopped inactive-chat tracker edits from calling Maps ('Failed to flush 1 game-state patch callback').
fix: Add Hierarchical Maps to references/architecture.md: mention it in the Game Mode/Roleplay sections as a downloadable Tracker Agent package (v2.3), its controls living inside Chat Settings -> Agents, that it obeys the Enable Agents master toggle (v2.3.3), and the 2.3.3 migration/quarantine fixes as known-issue context.

title: Downloadable Agents packaging rework missing
reality: v2.3.0 restructured the engine around downloadable capability packages: a full-page Agents -> Download Agents library (Writer/Tracker/Misc groupings, Install All/Uninstall All), first-party packages published in the Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents repo (canonical 29-package catalog), Hierarchical Maps, Calls, and all table games moved into optional packages with package-owned server runtimes, >25,000 lines removed from the base Engine leaving validated capability registries and compatibility bridges, fresh installs containing NO optional agents (existing installs migrate). v2.3.1 added startup auto-upgrade from the catalog with rollback; v2.3.2 added capability API 1.3 host services (#3690) and per-mode compatibility badges (#3676); v2.3.3 added compatibility-aware per-major catalog lanes (#3712).
fix: Add a 'Downloadable Agents / Capability Packages (v2.3)' section to references/architecture.md (Big Picture and/or a new section) covering the Download Agents library, the Marinara-Agents catalog repo, package-owned server runtimes, capability API 1.3 host services, fresh-installs-have-no-optional-agents, startup auto-update with rollback, and the migration behavior.

title: Agent object description stale after packaging split
reality: architecture.md's Agent core-object section says '22 built-ins plus user-defined custom agents.' Since v2.3.0 many former built-ins (Hierarchical Maps, Calls, table games, Music DJ, Illustrator, Card Evolution, Lorebook Keeper, etc.) are downloadable packages from a 29-package catalog; fresh installs ship with no optional agents; agent sections/settings/command toggles appear only for installed agents. v2.3.2 (#3692) also lets selected custom agents run in Conversation, Roleplay, and Game whenever Enable Agents is on.
fix: Rewrite the Agent core-object blurb: replace '22 built-ins' with the v2.3 model (built-in core + downloadable official packages from the Marinara-Agents catalog + custom agents), note fresh installs include no optional agents, and note custom agents can run in all three modes when Enable Agents is on (v2.3.2).

title: Turn games described as built-in shared engine
reality: In v2.3.0 UNO, Chess, Poker, 8-Ball Pool, Tic-Tac-Toe, and Rock-Paper-Scissors moved into optional downloadable packages with package-owned runtimes; installed games appear in the Commands controls without separate Add Agent entries (v2.3.0 fix) and activate/deactivate slash-command and runtime contributions without an Engine restart (v2.3.2 #3699).
fix: Update the Turn games bullet: note the six table games are now optional downloadable Conversation-game packages (v2.3.0), appear under Commands when installed, and hot-activate without restart (v2.3.2 #3699); the shared-engine path/route note should be qualified as the pre-2.3 layout.

title: Conversation Calls renamed Calls and now a package owning Local Whisper
reality: v2.3.0 moved Conversation audio/video calls into an optional downloadable package and made Local Whisper a Calls-owned download: Connections shows Local Speech Model controls only while the Calls package is installed, and uninstalling it deletes all downloaded Whisper models and the saved selection (reinstalling restores availability). v2.3.2 renamed user-facing 'Conversation Calls' to 'Calls' (#3676, package IDs and legacy symbols preserved) and shipped package v1.0.4 fixing hardcoded fallback replies (#3685); #3671 fixed Whisper model discovery when DATA_DIR is unset.
fix: In the 'Conversation Calls (v2.1)' block: rename to 'Calls' (noting the v2.3.2 rename and preserved package IDs/API route), state it is now a downloadable package (v2.3.0) rather than built-in, and note Local Whisper models are Calls-owned (uninstall removes them). Keep the /api/conversation-calls endpoint listing but note the user-facing rename.

title: Data Storage still documents SQLite backend and DATABASE_URL import
reality: v2.3.0 removed the retired database compatibility stack entirely: the runtime backend switch, startup migrations, one-time importer/repair readers, old migration scripts, database-file backup handling, and external ORM/runtime dependencies. Storage schemas and query expressions are file-native throughout, with file-native primary/natural-key constraints enforced during atomic inserts/updates; graceful-shutdown flush hardening landed in #3602 and capability packages resolve schemas by registered name (#3647).
fix: Rewrite the Data Storage opening: storage is file-native throughout the Engine as of v2.3.0 — remove the STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite opt-in and DATABASE_URL import claims (note them only as pre-2.3 history if at all), and optionally note file-native constraint enforcement and that downloaded packages access storage via registered schema names.

title: Conversation prompt assembly rework (v2.3.1) missing
reality: v2.3.1 reworked Conversation prompt assembly: Peek Prompt groups Conversation turns under a **Chat History** section, character join/leave notices become timestamped history events only after a chat has started, reaction syntax lives inside **Commands**, merged-group speaker-prefix and character-only response boundaries are emitted last in the preset's XML/Markdown/plain format, and the built-in Conversation prompt + Marinara preset use identity wording fitting both 1:1 and group chats (with a startup migration for old bundled presets).
fix: In Prompt Assembly, replace/extend the one-line Conversation description with a 'v2.3.1 Conversation assembly rework' note covering Chat History grouping, timestamped join/leave events, reaction syntax under Commands, last-emitted merged-group boundaries, and the preset identity-wording migration.

title: Group Conversation now one merged generation per turn
reality: v2.3.1 restored group chats to one merged provider generation per turn — the model chooses every present speaker within a single grouped response instead of separate restricted per-character requests (Roleplay Individual mode unchanged). v2.3.2 (#3673) fixed merged group prompts stripping speaker-tag examples.
fix: Update the 'Group DMs are supported' line: Conversation group chats run as a single merged generation per turn where the model picks all speakers (v2.3.1); Roleplay Individual mode remains per-character.

title: Conversation schedule timezone selector missing
reality: v2.3.1 added a global timezone selector to Conversation schedule creation: defaults to the browser-detected IANA timezone, overridable or resettable to the current device zone, syncs across devices, applies to existing and future Conversation chats; schedule generation, presence, autonomous messages, temporal prompt context, and background server polling honor it. v2.3.0 (#3590) also fixed blank TZ= handling to inherit the host timezone.
fix: In the Conversation Mode 'Schedules' bullet, add the v2.3.1 global IANA timezone selector (browser-detected default, device-syncing, honored by schedules/presence/autonomous messages/temporal context/polling).

title: Noodle refresh prompt now user-editable (Noodle Prompt)
reality: v2.3.0 added an editable **Noodle Prompt** at the top of Noodle Settings with a full-screen editor and one-click default restoration; the canonical default contains the complete adult-platform, persona-authorship, interaction, and JSON instructions, with the separate timeline voice text appended last.
fix: Update the Noodle 'Refresh (generation)' paragraph: the main refresh prompt is now an editable Noodle Prompt (v2.3.0, full-screen editor, restore-default), with the Timeline Voice & Tone text appended last; adjust the 'schema-critical rules stay hardcoded' claim accordingly.

title: Noodle participant selection and 8192-token budgets missing
reality: v2.3.2 changed Noodle refreshes to choose active participants BEFORE first-time profile generation, skip characters that already have generated profiles, and send only the selected character cards to the timeline model; world/lore context and chat carryover each get an 8,192-token budget so large invited rosters cannot inflate unrelated generations.
fix: In the Noodle 'Refresh (generation)' and/or 'Profiles' paragraphs, add the v2.3.2 behavior: participant selection precedes profile generation, only selected cards go to the model, and world/lore + chat-carryover context each have an 8,192-token budget.

title: Noodle persona authorship across switching
reality: v2.3.1 preserved distinct Noodle authorship across persona switching: posts and replies retain their originating persona account and snapshot, timeline prompts identify each persona by handle and stable identity key, and chat carryover summaries name the persona account instead of collapsing activity into the currently selected identity.
fix: In the Noodle 'Accounts' paragraph (which documents the in-Noodle account switcher), add that authorship is preserved per originating persona across switching (v2.3.1), including in timeline prompts and carryover summaries.

title: Professor Mari excluded from Noodle by default
reality: architecture.md lists Professor Mari as one of Noodle's accounts. v2.3.0 (#3598) added a default-ON setting that excludes Professor Mari from account discovery and future generated activity (existing timeline history is kept).
fix: In the Noodle 'Accounts' paragraph, note that a default-on setting (v2.3.0, #3598) excludes Professor Mari from discovery and future generated activity unless the user turns it off.

title: Persona fallback no longer applies to Roleplay
reality: v2.3.2 made new Roleplay chats stay persona-less when the user selects no Persona — including the first optimistic message snapshot, provider prompt, scene generation, and combat context; only Conversation mode may fall back to the globally active Persona.
fix: Add a caveat to the Persona core-object section (and/or Roleplay section): persona-less Roleplay chats remain persona-less throughout generation (v2.3.2); only Conversation falls back to the globally active persona.

title: Roleplay Summary truncation limits removed
reality: v2.3.2 removed Roleplay Summary's 2,000-character per-source-message truncation and the 64 KiB compiled-summary ceiling in chats.json; chapter-length messages and accumulated summaries stay complete unless the model rejects the request.
fix: In the 'Chat Summary (v2.2)' paragraph of the Roleplay section, add that v2.3.2 removed per-message and compiled-summary size ceilings, so summaries are bounded only by the model/connection limits.

title: Conversation routine-summary token ceiling raised to 8192
reality: v2.3.2 (#3696) raised Conversation routine-summary generations from a 512-token ceiling to an 8,192-token default, honors larger Connection overrides, and requests low reasoning effort so reasoning models return visible summaries.
fix: Add a note to the Conversation Mode section (near Schedules/memory features): routine summaries default to 8,192 output tokens (was 512), honor larger Connection overrides, and request low reasoning effort (v2.3.2, #3696).

title: About Me drafting moved to Professor Mari
reality: v2.3.2 moved Conversation About Me drafting from per-editor 'AI Write' controls to Professor Mari: Character and Persona Convo editors no longer expose a separate model connection or source settings; Mari inspects the saved character/persona, writes the bio in their voice, and saves directly to the About Me field. v2.3.0 also confirmed About Me and the update_about_me tool remain built into the Engine (not downloadable agents).
fix: In the Professor Mari section (and/or Conversation Mode), add that Mari now owns About Me drafting (v2.3.2) and that the About Me profile + update_about_me tool are Engine built-ins, not catalog packages.

title: Bot Browser renamed Card Browser / Download Cards
reality: v2.3.0 renamed 'Bot Browser' to 'Card Browser' throughout the interface, docs, onboarding, and Professor Mari guidance, and 'Browse Online' to 'Download Cards'; it opens as 'Cards Library' in the unified library shell.
fix: Rename user-facing 'Bot Browser' references to 'Card Browser' / 'Download Cards' (v2.3.0) in the Character section; keep the /api/bot-browser/* route path but note the UI rename.

title: Venice.ai image provider and NovelAI V4.5 style plates missing
reality: v2.3.2 (#3682) added Venice.ai as an Image Generation service (authenticated live model discovery, native /image/generate, model-aware sizing, validated base64 responses). v2.3.3 (#3725, #3726) added persistent NovelAI V4.5 style plates with independent strength/fidelity and subject-count framing selecting portrait/square/landscape dimensions.
fix: In Providers Supported, extend the image-gen line to include Venice.ai (v2.3.2) and optionally note the NovelAI V4.5 style-plate controls (v2.3.3).

title: Connections Defaults 'Illustrator' category renamed 'Images'
reality: v2.3.0 renamed the Connections Illustrator defaults category to **Images** (and renamed selfie configuration to 'Illustrator Settings' inside Chat Settings -> Agents, with image settings and /illustrate //selfie commands hidden until the Illustrator package is installed).
fix: Update the Connection Defaults sentence to 'Main, Agents, Images (renamed from Illustrator in v2.3.0), Videos' and note that Illustrator-dependent image commands/settings only appear when the Illustrator package is installed.

title: What's New window missing
reality: v2.3.0 added a one-time, version-aware 'What's New?' window for fresh installs and updates: waits until first-run onboarding completes, introduces each release's features with Professor Mari, links to the GitHub release, and remembers the exact version shown so it doesn't reappear until the next update.
fix: Add a bullet to 'Special Features Worth Knowing': version-aware What's New window (v2.3.0) shown once per update after onboarding, with release links.

title: Generation-completion notifications missing
reality: v2.3.0 (#3588) added separate opt-in browser and Android notifications for manually started Conversation, Roleplay, Visual Novel, and Game replies that finish while Marinara is unfocused, independent of autonomous-message background notification preferences.
fix: Add a bullet to 'Special Features Worth Knowing': opt-in generation-completion notifications (browser + Android) for manually started replies finishing while unfocused (v2.3.0, #3588).

title: New env vars CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED missing
reality: v2.3.3 (#3730) added CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS for slow Conversation/Roleplay/Game providers, and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=false for persistent launcher update opt-out on Windows, macOS/Linux, and Termux without disabling manual updates.
fix: Add these two env vars to references/architecture.md (e.g., alongside the existing env/config troubleshooting notes near VIDEO_GEN_TIMEOUT_MS): CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS (chat-generation timeout for slow providers) and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=false (launcher auto-update opt-out), both v2.3.3 #3730.

title: 'No plugin marketplace' claim now misleading
reality: Since v2.3.0 there IS an official in-app Download Agents catalog (Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents, 29 packages, install/update/uninstall, startup auto-update) for capability packages; only client Extensions remain manual CSS/JS.
fix: Reword the bullet: client Extensions remain manual CSS/JS with no third-party marketplace, but official capability packages ARE distributed via the in-app Download Agents catalog (v2.3.0) — third-party packages are not supported there.
